newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul opposition wants parliament to probe Hanbo.
newsitem.headline: Seoul opposition wants parliament to probe Hanbo.

text.p: South Korea's main opposition parties on Monday called for a parliamentary probe into the Hanbo Group, saying its financial woes were the country's biggest financial scandal.
President Kim Young-sam earlier ordered the government to open an investigation into Hanbo, whose steel unit defaulted on debt and is now seeking court protection along with three other affiliates.
"The Hanbo incident is the biggest ever power-linked financial irregularity," a statement said, adding it had "dealt a fatal shock" to the economy.

The statement was issued jointly by the National Congress for New Politics and United Liberal Democratic Party. It said the parties would probe the affair and called on parliament to open an investigation after it reconvenes.

The statement said it was not appropriate for state prosecutors to look into the Hanbo scandal in view of suspicions that the government pressured banks to provide huge loans to the Hanbo Group despite its shaky financial status.
